newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian currency falls 5.88 pct at market rate.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian currency falls 5.88 pct at market rate.

text.p: The central bank on Wednesday devalued Nigeria's naira currency at the free market, saying it would now exchange at 85 instead of 80 to the dollar.
"Foreign exchange will now be offered at the market rate of 85 to one US dollar," central spokesman Tony Ede told reporters in the capital Abuja.
The central bank is due to sell foreign exchange on Thursday on the automomous foreign exchange market (AFEM) where it auctions foreign currency weekly and the new rate will be applied there.

Demand for dollars at AFEM rose to more than $90 million last week from the normal weekly level of about $70 million and economists immediately warned that if not checked this could cause a crash in the value of the naira.
Bankers said that to check bogus demands, the central bank had called for detailed information on the end users of the foreign exchange that banks bought at the AFEM over the last one month.
Nigeria's military government maintains dual exchange rates with an official rate of 22 naira to $1 for a few government transactions including debt servicing.
International lending institutions and business have long criticised the system and called for a merger at the AFEM rate.

Ede said the fall in the value of the naira was due to a high liquidity level in the market and blamed this on the petroleum trust fund set up by goverment last year to use the proceeds of a 1994 fuel hike to rehabilitate public services.
"This new rate became necessary there is too much money in circulation," he said.
